tldr: A marginal modal treatment effect reports the displacement of the most likely potential outcome relative to an externally calibrated public control reference \(p_0\). On the committed class with known uniform continuous covariates, unknown H\"older-\(7/100\) assignment and treated conditional densities, two outcome derivatives, and public marginal curvature, the focal object is a single explicit rate governing both all-estimator absolute risk and finite-sample honest connected-interval length. The exact known-control restriction is a load-bearing benchmark: only the treated counterfactual mode is learned under rough continuous confounding. The rate and its logarithmic factors are research outputs. Observable correction of persistent nuisance drift, lawful normalized lower mixtures and public local calibration must deliver the same order on the full class. The result would determine whether the ordinary \(n^{-1/5}\) mode benchmark survives rough observational confounding. Estimating a second unknown control mode is a separate extension.
gap: \cite{Chang2020ModeTreatmentEffect} already defines the marginal causal modal contrast. Its first-order asymptotic theorem and the localized nuisance conditions of \cite{HamWestlingDoss2024CounterfactualLogconcave} do not establish the committed rough-class minimax and honest-length match. The exact known-control benchmark restriction is newly maintained here; Chang\textquotesingle s broader two-arm formulation is not precedent for that restriction.
fill: A total observable attainer and a direct same-class observed-experiment converse determine one explicit uncertainty rate for the treated counterfactual mode relative to the fixed control mode. A finite-sample calibration proof must account for smoothing bias, reciprocal remainders, random pilot weights and every local-process contribution. Estimating a second unknown control mode, or propagating uncertainty in external reference calibration, is a separate extension.
